thread:
alice: early this morning the preemptible gpu pool went into NotReady/NoSchedule after autoscaler added nodes.

ben: logs?

alice: grabbed kubelet / systemd output from one node:
```
Sep 07 03:01:58 kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
Sep 07 03:02:00 systemd: nvidia-modprobe.service: control process exited, code=exited status=1
Sep 07 03:02:12 kubelet[1234]: E0907 03:02:12.345 device_plugin.go: failed to start plugin: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create device plugin socket: dial unix /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: connect: no such file or directory
```

carla: sounds like kernel/driver mismatch — we deployed an image with 5.12 but drivers packaged for 5.11.

dave: autoscaler saw nodes join but never became Ready -> scaled up more. finance noted a preemptible +20% spend spike.

alice: temp fix: reinstalled driver on one node and restarted plugin, pods scheduled. commands i ran:
```
sudo apt-get update && sudo dpkg -i /opt/nvidia/nvidia-driver-470_470.57.02_amd64.deb
sudo depmod -a && sudo modprobe nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin
```

ben: can you put that into a runbook? we'll need an image rollback and a CI gate.

carla: agreed. proposed actions: 1) revert node image to kernel that matches driver 2) add CI test to boot a VM and modprobe nvidia as part of image publish 3) add readiness probe to device-plugin so node not considered Ready until socket exists 4) add autoscaler metric/visibility to show "nodes present but plugin missing".

alice: started drain+replace of faulty nodes at 03:12, new rolled-back nodes were Ready by 03:28, autoscaler scaled down by 03:36. cost impact estimated +18% for the hour.

dave: filed INFRA-3241..3243 in jira for the follow-ups.

ben: tagging @finance and @oncall. closing when postmortem up.

autoscaler-bot: "ScaledUp: +8 nodes (target 12 -> 20)"

autoscaler-bot: "ScaledDown: -7 nodes (20 -> 13)"

carla: closing thread once postmortem is attached.
